relevant_endpoints.summary: Returns templates filtered by Contract Type, Industry and/or Status; used both by Template Library listing and New Contract template selection
Searches existing counterparties by name, company or GST/Tax ID
Creates a new counterparty, blocking duplicates on GST/Tax ID
Returns tenant users filtered by role, used to populate Contract Owner dropdown
Uploads a third party paper file (PDF/DOCX, max 25MB) as an alternative to Template selection
Creates a new contract from a Template or uploaded third party paper, validates all mandatory and conditional fields, auto-fills merge fields, and saves as Draft

stories.title: Highlight Missing Mandatory Fields on Save
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be alerted when I leave a mandatory field blank and click Save, so that I can identify and complete all required information before the contract is created.
acceptance_criteria: Given the new contract creation form is open, When the user leaves one or more mandatory fields blank and clicks Save, Then the system displays the message 'Please fill all mandatory fields' and does not save the contract.
Given a mandatory field is left blank, When Save is clicked, Then the system highlights the missing field(s) in red so the user can identify them.

Given the mandatory fields include Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, and Due Date, When any of these is left blank and Save is clicked, Then the corresponding field is highlighted in red and the error message is displayed.

Given Template, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, and Notice Period are not universally mandatory, When these are left blank under conditions where they are not required, Then Save is not blocked on account of these fields.
Given Assigned Date is a system-generated, read-only label, When the user clicks Save, Then Assigned Date is never flagged as a missing mandatory field since it is auto-populated by the system.

Given all mandatory fields among Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date are correctly filled per their mandatory status, When the user clicks Save, Then no mandatory-field validation error is shown and the save proceeds.

stories.title: Prompt Upload of Third Party Paper When No Active Templates Exist
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be prompted to upload third party paper when no active templates exist for my selected Contract Type/Industry combination, so that I can still proceed with contract creation without being blocked by missing templates.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the New Contract Creation screen, when I select a Contract Type and Industry combination for which no active templates exist, then the system displays the message 'No active templates available for this combination. Please upload third party paper.' and disables the Template dropdown.

Given the system has displayed the no-active-templates message, when I proceed to complete the contract, then I must use the Upload Third Party Paper option instead of selecting a Template, and the Template field remains unavailable.

Given the no-active-templates message is displayed, when I continue entering contract details, then I must still be able to populate all remaining required data points: Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.

Given I have uploaded a third party paper after seeing the no-active-templates message, when I attempt to also select a Template, then the system prevents this because Template and Upload Third Party Paper remain mutually exclusive.
Given no active template exists and I have not uploaded third party paper, when I attempt to Save the contract, then the system blocks the save until a third party paper is uploaded.

stories.title: Block Save When End Date Precedes Start Date
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be blocked from saving a contract when the End Date is earlier than the Start Date, so that I avoid creating contracts with invalid date ranges.
acceptance_criteria: Given a contract form with Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date all populated, When the user enters a Start Date and then enters an End Date that is earlier than the Start Date, Then the system displays the error message 'End date cannot be earlier than start date'.
Given the End Date entered is earlier than the Start Date, When the user clicks Save, Then the Save action is blocked and the contract is not created.

Given the error 'End date cannot be earlier than start date' is displayed, When the user corrects the End Date to be later than the Start Date, Then the error is cleared and Save proceeds subject to validation of all other mandatory fields.

Given the End Date validation has failed, When the user reviews the form, Then all previously entered values for Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date remain intact and unaffected by the blocked Save.

stories.title: Block Save When Due Date Precedes Assigned Date
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be blocked from saving a contract when the Due Date is earlier than the Assigned Date, so that I avoid creating contracts with invalid scheduling data.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new contract form is open with Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, and Notice Period all populated as required, When the system-generated Assigned Date is displayed and the user sets a Due Date earlier than that Assigned Date, Then the system displays the error message 'Due date cannot be earlier than assigned date' and blocks the Save action.

Given the error message is displayed due to an invalid Due Date, When the user attempts to click Save without correcting the Due Date, Then the contract is not persisted and remains in an unsaved state.

Given the user corrects the Due Date to be on or after the Assigned Date, When all other mandatory fields including Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, and Renewal Type remain valid, When the user clicks Save, Then the error is cleared and the contract is saved successfully as Draft.

Given the Assigned Date field is read-only and auto-populated at creation, When the user attempts to directly edit the Assigned Date, Then the system prevents this edit, confirming only the Due Date comparison triggers this alternate flow.

stories.title: Reject Unsupported File Format on Third Party Paper Upload
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be alerted when I upload a third party paper file that is not PDF or DOCX, so that I can re-upload the file in a supported format and continue creating the contract.
acceptance_criteria: Given the New Contract Creation screen is displayed with fields Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date available for entry, when a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin selects the Upload Third Party Paper button and chooses a file that is not PDF or DOCX, then the system displays the message 'Unsupported file format. Please upload PDF or DOCX only.' and does not accept the file.

Given the unsupported file format error is displayed, when the user has not yet uploaded a valid PDF or DOCX file, then the Template field remains unaffected and the mutually exclusive relationship between Template and Upload Third Party Paper per BR-8 is preserved.

Given the unsupported file format error is displayed, when the user re-selects the upload control and chooses a file with a PDF or DOCX extension, then the error message is cleared and the file is accepted for upload.

Given the unsupported file upload error has been triggered, when the user proceeds to complete other fields such as Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, then the system continues to allow entry of these fields independently of the upload error.

Given no valid Template or third party paper has been provided due to the unsupported file format, when the user attempts to click Save, then the system blocks the Draft state transition per BR-14 until a valid Template is selected or a supported PDF/DOCX file is uploaded.

stories.title: Reject Oversized Third Party Paper Upload
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be alerted when my uploaded third party paper exceeds the 25 MB limit, so that I can upload a correctly sized file and continue entering contract details without data loss.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin is on the New Contract Creation screen with the Upload Third Party Paper option selected, When they attempt to upload a file larger than 25 MB, Then the system displays the message 'File size exceeds the 25 MB limit. Please upload a smaller file.' and does not accept the file.

Given the oversized file upload has been rejected, When the user reviews the form, Then all previously entered data points remain intact, including Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.
Given the file size error is displayed, When the user selects a file of 25 MB or less, Then the upload succeeds and the mutual exclusivity with Template selection is enforced per BR-8.

Given the oversized file error has occurred, When the user has not yet uploaded a valid file or selected a Template, Then the Save action remains blocked until either a valid Template or an acceptable third party paper is provided.

stories.title: Block Unauthorized User from Creating a Contract
stories.story_statement: As a user without the Contract Owner or Tenant Admin role, I want to be blocked from opening the New Contract Creation screen, so that I cannot access or populate contract creation fields I am not authorized to use.
stories.notes_assumptions: BR-13 indicates roles such as Legal Reviewer, Approver, External Party, and Signer are among those with no access; this alternate flow applies to any role outside Contract Owner and Tenant Admin.
acceptance_criteria: Given a logged-in user who does not hold the Contract Owner or Tenant Admin role for the current tenant, When the user attempts to open the New Contract Creation screen, Then the system displays the message 'You do not have permission to create a contract' and redirects the user to the Dashboard.

Given the user is redirected before the screen renders, When the redirection occurs, Then none of the following fields and data groups are displayed or made accessible to the user: Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.
Given the unauthorized access attempt, When the system blocks entry, Then no contract record or draft data is created for any of the above fields.
Given the user is redirected to the Dashboard, When the redirection completes, Then the user remains logged in to the application under their existing session and role.

stories.title: Prevent Duplicate Counterparty Creation via GST/Tax ID Match
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be alerted when the GST/Tax ID I enter matches an existing counterparty, so that I can select the existing record instead of creating a duplicate.
acceptance_criteria: Given the Add New Counterparty form is open, When the user enters a Counterparty GST/Tax ID that matches an existing counterparty's Tax ID, Then the system displays the message 'A counterparty with this Tax ID already exists' and shows the matching record for selection instead of creating a duplicate.

Given a matching counterparty record is displayed, When the user selects the matching record, Then the system populates the counterparty details from the existing record and does not create a new counterparty.

Given the duplicate Tax ID check has been triggered, When the user reviews the new contract form, Then the following data points remain available for entry or review on the screen: Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.

Given no existing counterparty matches the entered GST/Tax ID, When the user proceeds to save the new counterparty details, Then no duplicate warning is shown and the new counterparty is created normally.

stories.title: Filter Template Dropdown by Active Status, Contract Type, and Industry
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to see only Active templates filtered by the selected Contract Type and Industry in the Template dropdown, so that I can quickly select a valid, approved template for my new contract.
stories.notes_assumptions: The fourth acceptance criterion enumerates all 18 required data points as context fields present on the New Contract Creation screen per the extraction requirement, though BR-1 itself specifically governs only the Template, Contract Type, and Industry fields.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am on the New Contract Creation screen and have selected a Contract Type and an Industry, When the Template dropdown is populated, Then it displays only templates with status = Active that match both the selected Contract Type and Industry.
Given a template has status other than Active for the selected Contract Type and Industry combination, When I open the Template dropdown, Then that template is excluded from the list.

Given I change the Contract Type or Industry selection after the Template dropdown has been populated, When the change is applied, Then the Template dropdown refreshes to show only Active templates matching the newly selected Contract Type and Industry.

Given the New Contract Creation screen, When I review the data entry fields and groups involved in contract creation, Then the screen accounts for Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.

Given no template has status = Active for the selected Contract Type and Industry combination, When the Template dropdown is populated, Then it displays no selectable options, consistent with BR-2 behavior for blocking template selection.

stories.title: Block Template Selection and Prompt Third Party Paper Upload When No Active Template Exists
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want the system to block template selection and prompt me to upload a third party paper when no active template exists for the selected Contract Type/Industry combination, so that I can still proceed with contract creation without being stuck on an empty template list.
acceptance_criteria: Given I have selected a Contract Type [DP-UC2-001] and Industry [DP-UC2-002] combination for which no active Template [DP-UC2-003] exists, When the system evaluates the Template dropdown, Then the Template [DP-UC2-003] field is blocked/disabled and the system prompts me to upload a third party paper instead.

Given the Template selection is blocked due to no active template matching the Contract Type [DP-UC2-001] and Industry [DP-UC2-002], When I proceed with contract creation, Then I must upload a third party paper before continuing to enter Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009], Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010], Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011], Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], and Due Date [DP-UC2-020].

Given no active Template [DP-UC2-003] exists for the chosen Contract Type [DP-UC2-001] / Industry [DP-UC2-002] combination, When I attempt to select a Template anyway, Then the system prevents the selection and displays a message directing me to the Upload Third Party Paper option.

Given I have uploaded a third party paper in place of a blocked Template [DP-UC2-003], When I complete all remaining fields including Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009], Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010], Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011], Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], and Due Date [DP-UC2-020], Then I am able to save the contract as Draft.

stories.title: Reassign Contract Owner During Contract Creation
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want the Contract Owner field to default to me while still allowing reassignment to any valid Contract Owner within my tenant, so that contracts can be correctly attributed and managed by the appropriate user.
acceptance_criteria: Given the New Contract Creation screen is loaded with Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date fields available, When the screen first renders, Then the Contract Owner field defaults to the logged-in user.

Given the logged-in user holds the Contract Owner role, When the user opens the Contract Owner dropdown, Then only users holding the Contract Owner role within the same tenant are listed as selectable options alongside the logged-in user.

Given the Contract Owner field defaults to the logged-in user, When the Contract Owner selects a different eligible user from the dropdown, Then the Contract Owner field updates to the newly selected user and retains this value through Save.

Given a Tenant Admin is creating the contract, When the Tenant Admin opens the Contract Owner dropdown, Then the Tenant Admin can reassign the Contract Owner to any user holding the Contract Owner role within the same tenant.

Given the Contract Owner field is populated with a valid tenant user, When the user attempts to select a user from a different tenant, Then that user is not shown as an option in the Contract Owner dropdown.

stories.title: Enforce Notice Period Requirement Based on Renewal Type
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to Notice Period to become mandatory only when Renewal Type is Auto or Manual, and be disabled and cleared when Renewal Type is None, so that I do not enter inconsistent or irrelevant renewal data.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am creating a new contract and have selected Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, and End Date, When I set Renewal Type to Auto, Then Notice Period becomes mandatory and must be entered before Save succeeds, with Assigned Date and Due Date still governed by their own rules.

Given I am entering the same contract details (Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date), When I set Renewal Type to Manual, Then Notice Period becomes mandatory and must be entered before Save succeeds.

Given I have entered a Notice Period value while Renewal Type was Auto or Manual, When I change Renewal Type to None, Then the Notice Period field is disabled and its previously entered value is cleared.

Given Renewal Type is set to None, When I attempt to click Save with Notice Period left blank, Then Save proceeds without requiring Notice Period, provided all other mandatory fields (Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Due Date) are valid and Assigned Date is auto-populated.
Given Renewal Type is Auto or Manual and Notice Period is left blank, When I click Save, Then the system blocks saving and displays a validation error indicating Notice Period is required.

stories.title: Auto-Generate Read-Only Assigned Date on Contract Creation
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want the Assigned Date to be automatically generated as the current date and locked from editing, so that the contract's creation timestamp remains accurate and tamper-proof.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin begins creating a new contract, When the contract creation screen loads, Then the Assigned Date field is auto-populated with the current system date and displayed as a read-only label.

Given the contract creation form is displayed with fields Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, When the Contract Owner or Tenant Admin attempts to edit the Assigned Date field, Then the system prevents any modification and the field remains disabled for input.

Given the user attempts to edit Assigned Date via direct API call or browser manipulation, When the request is submitted, Then the system rejects the change and retains the original system-generated Assigned Date.
Given the contract is saved as Draft, When Due Date is validated against Assigned Date, Then the Due Date must be on or after the unmodified, system-generated Assigned Date.

stories.title: Block Due Date entries earlier than Assigned Date
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be blocked from entering a Due Date earlier than the Assigned Date, so that contract scheduling remains logically consistent.
acceptance_criteria: Given a contract creation form with the full field set including Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, When the Assigned Date is system-generated as the current date, Then the Due Date field must default to accept only dates on or after that Assigned Date.

Given the user enters a Due Date earlier than the Assigned Date, When they attempt to Save the contract, Then the system blocks the save action and displays an error indicating Due Date cannot be earlier than Assigned Date.
Given the user enters a Due Date on or after the Assigned Date, When they attempt to Save the contract, Then the system accepts the Due Date and proceeds without error.

Given all mandatory fields (Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Due Date) plus conditional fields (Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Template, Notice Period, Assigned Date) are reviewed, When the Due Date validation fails, Then Save is blocked regardless of the validity of other fields.

stories.title: Block Save When End Date Is Not Later Than Start Date
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to be blocked from saving a contract when the End Date is not later than the Start Date, so that contract duration data remains logically valid.
acceptance_criteria: Given a new contract form with all other mandatory fields completed, including Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, When the user enters an End Date that is earlier than or equal to the Start Date, Then the system blocks Save and displays an error indicating End Date must be later than Start Date.

Given a new contract form with all other mandatory fields completed, including Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, When the user enters an End Date that is later than the Start Date, Then the system allows Save to proceed and the contract is saved as Draft.
Given the user has entered a Start Date, When the user attempts to set an End Date equal to the Start Date, Then the system treats this as invalid and blocks Save.
Given a validation error is shown for End Date versus Start Date, When the user corrects the End Date to be later than the Start Date, Then the error clears and Save becomes available.

stories.title: Enforce Mutual Exclusivity Between Template Selection and Third Party Paper Upload
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want selecting a Template to disable the Upload Third Party Paper option (and vice versa), so that I cannot create a contract from two conflicting document sources at once.
stories.notes_assumptions: Data points beyond Template and Upload Third Party Paper are listed to satisfy the coverage requirement, confirming they remain unaffected by this mutual-exclusivity rule.
acceptance_criteria: Given the New Contract Creation screen is open with Contract Type and Industry selected, when I select a value in the Template dropdown, then the Upload Third Party Paper button is disabled and cannot be clicked.
Given the New Contract Creation screen is open, when I click Upload Third Party Paper and successfully attach a file, then the Template dropdown is disabled and cannot be used to select a template.

Given a Template has been selected and the Upload Third Party Paper option is disabled, when I clear or change the Template selection to none, then the Upload Third Party Paper option becomes enabled again.
Given a third party paper has been uploaded and the Template dropdown is disabled, when I remove the uploaded file, then the Template dropdown becomes enabled again.

Given the mutual exclusivity rule is active on either Template or Upload Third Party Paper, when I enter the remaining contract fields, then Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date remain independently editable per their own field rules and are unaffected by the Template/Upload exclusivity.
Given neither Template nor Upload Third Party Paper has been selected, when the screen loads, then both options are enabled and available for selection.

stories.title: Auto-populate template merge fields from entered contract data on save
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to have the merge fields in my selected template auto-populated from the data I entered on Save, so that the generated document accurately reflects the contract details without manual rework.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin has selected an active Template and entered contract details, When the user clicks Save, Then the system populates the template's merge fields using the entered values before generating the document.

Given the contract form has been filled out, When Save is clicked, Then the merge fields populated in the generated document include Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.

Given a field such as Counterparty Address or Notice Period is left blank because it was not mandatory or not applicable, When the document is generated, Then the corresponding merge field is left blank or omitted without blocking generation.
Given the Assigned Date is system-generated and read-only, When Save is clicked, Then the Assigned Date merge field is populated with the system-generated date rather than any user-entered value.

Given all mandatory fields (including Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, and Due Date) are validly entered, When Save is clicked, Then the document is generated only after all merge fields have been populated from the entered data.

stories.title: Set New Contract to Draft Status on Creation
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to have every newly created contract automatically set to Draft status regardless of its creation method, so that I have a consistent and predictable starting state for all contracts before further processing.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin has selected a Template and entered Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date and Due Date, When the contract is saved, Then the contract status is set to Draft.

Given a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin has uploaded a third party paper instead of selecting a Template and entered Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date and Due Date, When the contract is saved, Then the contract status is set to Draft.

Given a contract has been created via either a Template or an uploaded third party paper, When the save operation completes successfully, Then the resulting Draft status is identical in both cases with no variation based on the creation method.

Given a newly created contract is in Draft status, When the user views the contract immediately after save, Then no other status (e.g., Active, Pending Review) is displayed regardless of which fields among Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date and Due Date were populated.

stories.title: Create and Save a New Contract as Draft Without Editing Template or Clause Library
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to create a new contract by selecting a template or uploading third party paper, searching or adding counterparties, and entering all contract details, so that I can save a complete contract as Draft without being able to modify the tenant's template or clause library.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as Contract Owner on the New Contract screen, When I choose to use a template, Then I must select Contract Type, Industry, and Template, and the Upload Third Party Paper option becomes disabled.

Given I am logged in as Contract Owner on the New Contract screen, When I choose to upload third party paper instead of a template, Then the Template field is disabled and I can proceed without selecting a Template.

Given I need to associate a counterparty, When I use Counterparty Search and no match is found, Then I can add a new counterparty by entering Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, and Counterparty GST/Tax ID.

Given I am entering contract details, When I complete the form, Then I must provide Contract Type, Industry, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, and Due Date, while Assigned Date is auto-populated and read-only, and Notice Period is required only if Renewal Type is Auto or Manual.

Given all mandatory fields including Contract Type, Industry, Template (or uploaded paper), Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period (where applicable), Assigned Date, and Due Date are valid, When I click Save, Then the contract is created and its status is set to Draft.
Given I am on the New Contract screen, When I look for options to edit the tenant's template or clause library, Then no such editing controls are available to me as Contract Owner on this screen.

stories.title: Create contract on behalf of another Contract Owner
stories.story_statement: As a Tenant Admin, I want to create a new contract on behalf of any Contract Owner and reassign the Contract Owner field to any tenant user, so that I can manage contract creation across the tenant without being restricted to my own ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as a Tenant Admin, When I access the New Contract screen, Then I have the same entry rights as a Contract Owner for all fields: Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date.
Given I am creating a new contract, When I view the Contract Owner dropdown, Then I can reassign the Contract Owner field to any user within the current tenant, not just myself.
Given I have selected a different Contract Owner, When I complete and save the contract, Then the contract is created on behalf of that selected Contract Owner.
Given I am a Tenant Admin, When I attempt to edit the tenant's template or clause library from this screen, Then the system blocks this action, consistent with Contract Owner entry rights.

Given I am a Tenant Admin, When I enter all mandatory data points including Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, Then I can save the contract as Draft.

stories.title: Block Restricted Roles from Accessing New Contract Creation Screen
stories.story_statement: As a Legal Reviewer, I want to be denied access to the New Contract Creation screen, so that contract creation remains restricted to authorized roles and screen fields are not exposed to unauthorized users.
acceptance_criteria: Given a user logged in with the Legal Reviewer, Approver, External Party, or Signer role, When they attempt to navigate to the New Contract Creation screen, Then access is denied and the screen containing Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date is not rendered.

Given a Legal Reviewer, Approver, External Party, or Signer attempts to access the New Contract Creation screen via direct URL or deep link, When the request is processed, Then the system blocks the request and none of the fields Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, or Due Date is accessible or editable.

Given a user with Contract Owner or Tenant Admin role is logged in, When they access the New Contract Creation screen, Then they are permitted to view and enter Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, confirming the restriction applies only to the excluded roles.

stories.title: Restrict Draft Transition to Valid Save by Authorized Roles
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want the contract to transition from None to Draft only when I click Save with all mandatory fields valid, so that incomplete or unauthorized contracts are never persisted into the system.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in as Contract Owner or Tenant Admin and have completed all mandatory fields, When I click "Save", Then the contract state transitions from None to Draft.

Given I am logged in as Contract Owner or Tenant Admin, When I click "Save" and any mandatory field among Contract Type, Industry, Counterparty Search (or added counterparty details), Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, or Due Date is missing or invalid, Then the Save action is blocked and the contract remains in None state with an error indicating the missing/invalid field.
Given a user without Contract Owner or Tenant Admin role attempts to trigger the Save action, When the action is invoked, Then the state transition from None to Draft is blocked.

Given the mandatory fields Contract Type, Industry, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, and Due Date are all valid, and the optional/conditional fields Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Notice Period, and Assigned Date are populated or correctly left blank as applicable, When "Save" is clicked, Then the contract transitions to Draft and all entered data points including Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date are persisted correctly.
Given Notice Period is mandatory due to Renewal Type being Auto or Manual, When Save is clicked without Notice Period populated, Then Save is blocked as a mandatory field violation.
Given Assigned Date is a system-generated, read-only label, When Save is clicked, Then Assigned Date is auto-populated and not treated as a missing mandatory field validation failure.

stories.title: Restrict Contract State to Draft After Save
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to have the contract's state remain fixed at Draft once saved, so that no unintended state transitions occur on the New Contract Creation screen.
acceptance_criteria: Given a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin has entered Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date, When the contract is saved, Then the contract's state is set to Draft and no other state value is possible from this screen.

Given a contract has already been saved and its state is Draft, When the Contract Owner or Tenant Admin revisits the New Contract Creation screen or re-saves the same data, Then the state remains Draft and no further state transition is triggered from this screen.

Given the contract is in Draft state after save, When any user attempts to transition the contract to a state other than Draft (e.g., In Review, Approved) from this screen, Then the system blocks the transition, since such transitions are only supported in later use cases.

Given the contract fields Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, and Due Date have been successfully captured and saved, When the Save action completes, Then the resulting contract record persists with state Draft only.

stories.title: Validate Contract Creation Form Fields
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to have all Contract Creation Form fields validated according to their defined rules, so that I can create an accurate and complete contract record without errors.
acceptance_criteria: Given the Contract Creation Form is displayed, When I view the field set, Then the following fields/data groups must each be present and individually validated per their rules: Contract Type, Industry, Template, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, Due Date.

Given I attempt to save the form without selecting a value, When Contract Type, Industry, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, or Due Date is left empty, Then the system blocks Save and displays a mandatory field error for each missing field.

Given I select a Contract Type and Industry, When I open the Template dropdown, Then only active templates matching the selected Contract Type and Industry are displayed, and Template is not required if a third party paper is uploaded.
Given I enter a Counterparty Email, When the value does not match a valid email format, Then the system displays a format validation error and blocks save until corrected.

Given I am adding a new counterparty, When Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, or Counterparty Company is left blank, Then the system marks these as required and blocks counterparty addition; Counterparty Address remains optional and Counterparty GST/Tax ID is checked for duplicates.
Given I set Start Date and End Date, When End Date is not later than Start Date, Then the system displays a validation error and blocks Save.

Given I select Renewal Type as Auto or Manual, When Notice Period is left blank, Then the system requires a whole-number day value for Notice Period before allowing Save; if Renewal Type is None, Notice Period is disabled and cleared.
Given the contract is being created, When the form loads, Then Assigned Date is auto-populated as read-only in DD/MM/YYYY format and cannot be edited.
Given I enter a Due Date, When the Due Date is earlier than the Assigned Date, Then the system blocks entry with an error.

stories.title: Validate Counterparty Panel and Related Contract Fields
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to search for or add a counterparty and have all related contract fields validated according to their rules, so that I can only save a contract once mandatory and conditional field requirements are correctly satisfied.
stories.notes_assumptions: Although this coverage unit's description focuses on the Counterparty Panel fields (F-5 to F-11), the acceptance criteria also enumerate the remaining required data points (DP-UC2-001 through DP-UC2-020) per the coverage requirement that every listed data point be named explicitly.
acceptance_criteria: Given the New Contract Creation screen is open, When the user attempts to proceed without entering a value in Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Then the system blocks progress and flags Counterparty Search as mandatory.

Given the user clicks Add New Counterparty, When the counterparty entry fields open, Then Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], and Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009] become mandatory while Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010] and Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011] remain optional.

Given a new counterparty is being added, When the user enters a value in Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008] that does not conform to email format, Then the system displays a validation error and blocks saving.

Given a new counterparty is being added, When the user enters a Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011] that matches an existing counterparty's GST/Tax ID, Then the system flags the entry as a potential duplicate.

Given the contract form is being completed, When the user reviews or edits Contract Type [DP-UC2-001], Industry [DP-UC2-002], and Template [DP-UC2-003], Then the Template list is restricted to active templates matching the selected Contract Type and Industry.

Given the contract form is being completed, When the user enters Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], and Due Date [DP-UC2-020], Then each field is validated per its own mandatory, format, and conditional rules before Save is allowed.

Given all mandatory counterparty and contract fields listed (Contract Type [DP-UC2-001], Industry [DP-UC2-002], Template [DP-UC2-003], Counterparty Search [DP-UC2-005], Counterparty Name [DP-UC2-007], Counterparty Email [DP-UC2-008], Counterparty Company [DP-UC2-009], Counterparty Address [DP-UC2-010], Counterparty GST/Tax ID [DP-UC2-011], Contract Owner [DP-UC2-012], Contract Value [DP-UC2-013], Currency [DP-UC2-014], Start Date [DP-UC2-015], End Date [DP-UC2-016], Renewal Type [DP-UC2-017], Notice Period [DP-UC2-018], Assigned Date [DP-UC2-019], Due Date [DP-UC2-020]) are correctly populated, When the user clicks Save, Then the contract is created successfully without validation errors.

stories.title: Create a New Contract from Template or Third Party Paper and Save as Draft
stories.story_statement: As a Contract Owner, I want to create a new contract by selecting a template or uploading a third party paper, entering counterparty and contract details, and saving it, so that the contract is generated and stored as a Draft ready for further processing.
acceptance_criteria: Given I am logged in with a Contract Owner or Tenant Admin role, when I click 'New Contract' on the Dashboard, then the system displays the New Contract Creation screen with the Contract Type dropdown active.
Given the New Contract Creation screen is displayed, when I select Contract Type, then Industry, then a filtered active Template, then the system loads a template preview and merge fields.

Given I search for a counterparty, when I select an existing counterparty or click 'Add New Counterparty', then the system displays fields for Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, and Counterparty GST/Tax ID for entry.
Given a Counterparty Search has been performed, when results are returned, then matching existing counterparty records are displayed in a results list.
Given the Contract Owner field is populated, when I confirm or change it, then the system validates the selected owner holds the Contract Owner role in the tenant.

Given I am entering contract details, when I input Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, and Notice Period, then the system validates that End Date is after Start Date and Notice Period is a whole number.
Given the Assigned Date is auto-populated, when I review it and edit the Due Date, then the system validates that Due Date is not earlier than Assigned Date.
Given I choose not to use a Template, when I click 'Upload Third Party Paper' and select a PDF or DOCX file, then the system validates the file type and size and attaches it in place of a Template.

Given all mandatory fields (Contract Type, Industry, Template or Third Party Paper, Counterparty Search, Counterparty Name, Counterparty Email, Counterparty Company, Counterparty Address, Counterparty GST/Tax ID, Contract Owner, Contract Value, Currency, Start Date, End Date, Renewal Type, Notice Period, Assigned Date, Due Date) are valid, when I click 'Save', then the system auto-fills the merge fields, generates the contract document, sets the status to Draft, and displays 'Contract created successfully and saved as Draft'.
